conclusion: A flexible, bending-elastic cord (~0.70 m, ~1 cm thick) lying on a table, one end held by the tool. It slides quickly when pulled taut and fast (the whole straight cord moved at 3.5 m/s with the tool), stops within ~0.1 s when the motion has to bend it, and after any throw re-straightens slowly (0.3-0.5 m/s over 1.5-2 s) along the direction of its near part. The task is to throw (cast/flick) it so the free end comes to rest in a disc placed 0.12 m straight behind a short post, out of the tool's reach. Extended run: a full-rate stroke of >= 0.25 m with an immediate haul, on a straight cord aligned so its centroid lies straight behind the cast line, throws the tip into the target disc reliably on one situation (7 of the 8 casts of >= 0.23 m on seed 62 passed 0.054-0.135 m from its centre), but the cord turns over at a flight chord of 0.61 m and recoils, or grazes the post and collapses; a follow-through softens the recoil. Few layouts leave room for the needed stroke, and nothing made the tip come to rest in the disc.

field_note.one_go: once thrown, the cord can only be pulled back (and slow pulls only move a taut tip towards the tool); a second throw needs the cord behind the tool again
field_note.slowly_nowhere: confirmed in life 4: slow tool paths leave the tip where it is; only a fast, taut throw moves the cord beyond the zone
field_note.small_change: confirmed: the end direction depends on how the near part ends up after the hairpin (life 5: 54 deg off), which shifts with small changes of stroke and initial curl
